findings.title: Device limit is bypassed on the second request: local cache is populated before the store rejects the device
findings.body: In `tagDeviceUI` the device cache key is written with `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` *before* `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice` is called. When the store returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` (device not inserted), the cache entry remains for ~29 minutes. On the very next request from the same device ID, `tagDeviceUI` hits the cache and returns nil, so `TagDevice` returns nil and `Anonymous.Authenticate` issues an anonymous identity. The result is that a device over the limit is rejected exactly once and then admitted on refresh/retry, without ever being counted in the DB. The limit is therefore effectively unenforced (any number of devices can get in with two requests each). The cache entry must only be set after a successful create/update (or be deleted on error).

findings.title: DI signature change for ProvideAnonymousDeviceService/ProvideAnonDBStore without updating the wire provider set
findings.body: `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` previously accepted `anonstore.AnonStore`, which means the production wire graph had a provider for it (`anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` bound to `AnonStore`). This PR changes `ProvideAnonDBStore` to require an `int64` device limit and makes `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` take `db.DB` instead, but `pkg/server/wire.go` is not among the changed files. If the old provider/bind is still listed, `wire gen` fails (no provider for `int64`, or unused provider error), breaking the server build. The wire provider set must drop `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` and its bind (or the store should keep taking `*setting.Cfg`).

findings.title: Count-then-insert limit check is not atomic; concurrent new devices can exceed the configured limit
findings.body: `CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs `CountDevices` in one session and then the upsert in a separate `WithDbSession` call, with no transaction or lock. If N new devices arrive concurrently while the count is just below `deviceLimit`, all N read a count below the limit and all insert, so the stored active-device count exceeds the configured limit. The limit is only approximate under load. A single transaction with an appropriate lock, or a conditional insert (`INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) ...) < ?`), would make it enforceable.

findings.title: updateDevice mutates captured args inside the WithDbSession callback, which breaks on SQLite lock retries
findings.body: `updateDevice` does `args = append([]interface{}{query}, args...)` inside the closure passed to `WithDbSession`. The sqlstore's `retryOnLocks` re-invokes the same callback when SQLite returns `database is locked/busy` (when `query_retries` > 0), so on retry `args` becomes `[query, query, clientIP, ...]`: the SQL string is passed as the first bind parameter and the parameter count no longer matches the placeholders, so the retry fails with a driver error instead of succeeding. The same anti-pattern exists in `CreateOrUpdateDevice`; the new function copies it. Build the full argument slice outside the closure (or construct it fresh inside without reassigning the captured variable).

findings.title: ErrDeviceLimitReached is a plain error, so rejected users receive a generic unauthenticated response with no reason
findings.body: `Anonymous.Authenticate` returns the bare `fmt.Errorf("device limit reached")` from the store. The authn service joins client errors and the context handler simply treats the request as unauthenticated, redirecting to the login page with no message; the frontend has no way to distinguish 'device limit reached' from any other anonymous auth failure, and `anonymousDeviceLimit` in frontend settings does not help since the limit value alone does not indicate that this device was rejected. Returning an `errutil` error with a public message (as other authn clients do) would let the API/login page surface the actual reason.

findings.title: Device tagging moved from fire-and-forget to the synchronous request path even when no limit is configured
findings.body: Previously `TagDevice` ran in a goroutine with its own 2-minute timeout so anonymous authentication never waited on the device store. It now runs inline inside `Authenticate` on every local-cache miss (COUNT(*) + upsert, two DB round trips) regardless of whether `device_limit` is set. On anonymous-heavy deployments (public dashboards) with a slow or contended DB this adds request latency and makes anonymous auth fail/hang with the DB even when the operator never enabled the limit. Consider keeping the async path when `deviceLimit == 0`, or at least bounding the DB call with a short timeout.

findings.title: anonymousDeviceLimit is typed as `undefined` on GrafanaBootConfig although the backend always sends a number
findings.body: `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined;` without a type annotation makes TypeScript infer the property type as literally `undefined` under strict mode. The Go DTO emits `anonymousDeviceLimit` as an `int64` without `omitempty`, so at runtime it is always a number (0 when disabled). Consumers of the public `config` object cannot write `config.anonymousDeviceLimit > 0` without a cast, and the `number | undefined` declared in `GrafanaConfig` does not match the actual contract (0 = disabled, never undefined). Declare it as `anonymousDeviceLimit = 0;` (or `number | undefined` explicitly) and document that 0 means no limit.

findings.title: No test covers the limit through TagDevice/Authenticate, nor the update-at-limit path
findings.body: `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only verifies that a second *new* device at limit=1 returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` directly from the store. There is no test that (a) an already-registered device can still be updated when the limit is reached (the `updateDevice` success path), (b) a rejected device stays rejected on a subsequent `TagDevice`/`Authenticate` call (which would have caught the local-cache bypass in `tagDeviceUI`), or (c) `Anonymous.Authenticate` actually returns an error for an over-limit device. `impl_test.go` was only updated for the signature change and always uses `setting.NewCfg()` with limit 0.

findings.title: New `[auth.anonymous] device_limit` setting is not added to defaults.ini, sample.ini or the configuration docs
findings.body: The PR introduces a new ini key `device_limit` under `[auth.anonymous]` but does not add it to `conf/defaults.ini`, `conf/sample.ini`, or `docs/sources/setup-grafana/configure-grafana/_index.md`, which is the repository convention for every configuration option. Operators have no discoverable way to learn about the option, its default (0 = unlimited), or its semantics (devices active in the last 30 days). The PR description is also left as the unfilled template.
